newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak parliament approves new bank privatisation law.
newsitem.headline: Slovak parliament approves new bank privatisation law.

text.p: The Slovak parliament on Wednesday approved a new privatisation law which effectively allows the sell-off of state stakes in banks IRB and VUB.

The law had been returned to parliament by President Michal Kovac after it originally halted any sell-off of the two banks, as well as savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna and insurer Slovenska Poistovna.
Under the new law, the privatisation of Poistovna and Sporitelna will wait at least until the next general elections, planned for 1998.
"We gave political guarantees to the ZRS (Workers' Party) that Sporitelna and Poistovna will not be privatised until the end of this term," Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik told parliament.
"However, many OECD representatives have expressed concern over the (original) law saying it will make a number of complications for Slovak membership in the OECD," he added.
The new law was approved by a large majority, with 124 of the deputies present voting in favour, three against, and 12 abstentions. Four deputies did not vote at all.
The original law suspending bank privatisation was approved last month after the ultra-left ZRS, a junior partner in the ruling coalition, crossed the floor to vote in tandem with the opposition.
The opposition had called for the banks to be restructured before selling the state's stake.
Kozlik added that the government has a restructuring plan for the banks, but that it expects money to finance the plan to come from revenues generated by the banks' privatisation.

Through the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, the state controls 91.3 percent of Slovenska Sporitelna, 50.5 percent Slovenska Poistovna, some 35 percent in IRB and about 51.49 percent in VUB.
